question.worked_solution:
The integral is defined over a type I region.

First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $y$, treating $x$ as a constant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{-x}^{3x}\sqrt{x+y}\,dy\,dx & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{-x}^{3x}\sqrt{x+y}\,dy]\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{[\frac{2}{3}(x+y)^{3/2}]}_{-x}^{3x}\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(\frac{2}{3}(x+3x)^{3/2}-\frac{2}{3}(x-x)^{3/2})\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{2}{3}(4x)^{3/2}\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{16}{3}{x}^{3/2}\,dx \\  & =\frac{16}{3}{\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{3/2}\,dx\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{16}{3}{\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{3/2}\,dx & =\frac{16}{3}{[\frac{2}{5}{x}^{5/2}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{16}{3}(\frac{2}{5}-0) \\  & =\frac{32}{15}\end{aligned}
$$
